citation: Ekici M, Çakır Biçer N, Yirün A, Demirel G, Erkekoğlu P. Evaluation of Exposure to Bisphenol Analogs through Canned and Ready-to-Eat Meal Consumption and Their Possible Effects on Blood Pressure and Heart Rate. Nutrients. 2024;16(14):2275.
protocol: One meal per group: fresh, canned or plastic-packaged ready-to-eat (bean pilaki 200 g, stuffed grape leaves 100 g, corn 100 g, chicken 100 g, tomato 100 g); SBP, DBP, HR at 0, 2, 4, 6 h (0 h = pre-meal). No macronutrient or energy grams printed.
population: 48 healthy university students (24 male, 24 female), aged 18-30, BMI 18.5-24.9 by inclusion; 16 per meal group (8 M, 8 F); group mean BMI 21.7-22.0 (SD about 2.2); no chronic illness, normotensive, no medication.
note: Bisphenol-exposure study; BP and HR are the secondary outcome. Watch: meal composition is given only as food masses (Table 2), with no carbohydrate, fat or protein grams, so macros need a food table; 0 h values are pre-meal baseline. Table 4 also prints median, min and max; the SD is the stated spread.
